# name: #   xfail: a KNOWN defect, excused only at its exact wrong value: column 7
#   is an ERE matched only against a failure-verdict line (a line matching
#   ' FAIL ' or '^FAIL '), not against arbitrary log noise.  A regex that
#   hits only a debug line does not excuse a different failure.
#   If the row passes it is XPASS and FAILS, so a fix
#   forces the row back to "pass" (run.sh usage).  No waivers: rows are
#   pass, xfail-at-exact-value, or a gate listed in the lane manifest
#   (an xfail row with no gate writes "-" in the gate column: empty tab
#   fields collapse when run.sh reads the row)
# workers: - = live systemd iked; 0 = inline; N = pool
# gate: (empty) | addke  — gate=addke rows run only when the build supports
#   RFC 9370 ADDKE (R2_ADDKE=yes, i.e. the xfrm-addke build / OpenSSL 3.5 /
#   Fedora 44); they auto-SKIP on an OpenSSL 3.0 Ubuntu build.  This is what
#   keeps the PQC matrix off Ubuntu and on Fedora.
# Adding a case is a row. Kind scripts live in kinds/<kind>.sh
# Every ikev2/ikev1 tunnel row also runs fwd_tmpl_check: the Linux FWD
# policy must mirror the IN tmpl (e2bd9ef) or SSH-to-LAN dies quietly.

CREATECHILD mid-handler duplicate unit (review #5): netem duplicate 100% on the INITIATOR egress veth after child-up, so the rekey CREATE_CHILD REQUEST arrives twice back-to-back.  Dispatch (ikev2.c:538) short-circuits the second copy BEFORE the handler: pre-arm -> check_message_ordering sees recv_message_id advanced -> dropping-unordered; post-arm -> R2 replay.  Gate: exactly ONE 'CREATE_CHILD_SA request' handler entry (resp log, scoped to the rekey msgid) AND rekey completes (new SPI both sides) AND no abort AND (marker lines unordered+R2replay+frag-drop >= 1 OR a tcpdump -X msgid scan counts >= 2 msgid-M request packets on the responder-ingress tap — the wire count is the direct duplicate-arrival measurement and substitutes when the pre-arm drop path stays silent; box 2026-09-26 proved markers can be 0 with a completed rekey).  Two handler entries = the window hole is real.  Classical ESP (no ADDKE followup): the reassembler stores SKF fragments unconditionally (ikev2_frag.c:765) with a count-based completion (:778), so a duplicated mid-list fragment livelocks assembly and an ADDKE dup row would fail for the wrong reason.  DPD/NAT-D reply path unreachable (no yield between advance and arm) — documented, not a row.  gate=box: box-only until a container run passes.

RFC 7296 s1.4/s3.10.1 rekey-collision recovery: establish iked<->iked child, then the responder ikedctl delete-sa <peer> esp silently orphans it (kernel SAs dropped, child EXPIRED, no DELETE on the wire). The initiator's 45s ESP lifetime soft-expires and rekeys the OLD child SPI, which the responder no longer holds -> responder MUST answer CHILD_SA_NOT_FOUND (44) and the initiator aborts the doomed child (releasing its reserved SPI), clearing the stuck rekey. Kind also proves the delete-sa [esp|ah] selector: delete-sa ah on the ESP child prunes nothing. Gate: responder 'can't find corresponding child_sa' + initiator 'received Notify ... type CHILD_SA_NOT_FOUND' + initiator 'child aborted in state WAIT_RESPONSE' AND R esp pruned 2->0 by the esp delete. A clean rekey with nothing pruned proves nothing -> FAIL. Classical ESP (no ADDKE). Promoted to CI 2026-10-24 after 3/3 consecutive passes in an isolated two-netns run (kernel 6.12).

RFC 7383/7296 s2.2 replay unit (F10): i2ike-addke with initiator initial_child_ke immediate, so the IKE_AUTH child is rekeyed at once and the ML-KEM-768 IKE_FOLLOWUP_KE request goes out as several SKF fragments. tools/ikeframes.py taps the responder veth (AF_PACKET). After the responder has answered the next request (the DELETE at id F+1), the followup fragments (id F) are re-sent byte for byte from the initiator veth. Gate: the fragments reach iked (SKF recv lines grow by the number sent), the reassembled request is dropped by the window ("dropping unordered message (id F)"), the followup handler is not re-entered (no new "IKE_FOLLOWUP_KE msgid F (window at" or STATE_NOT_FOUND line), the SA survives, and nothing aborts. Needs python3.

PQC REQUEST-direction loss kill-test (review #4): every existing loss row drops responder->initiator only.  This row nets the INITIATOR egress veth (100% loss KEPT until the netem drop counter ticks — the counted loss of the first request copy — held ~4s so the 1s/3s ladder rungs are counted too, then qdisc REMOVED so the 7s rung arrives and FOLLOWUP+response ride the 10s ADDKE arm timer clean; dpd_delay 60 cannot pollute the window: earliest initiator DPD leaves after the qdisc is gone); recovery is the INITIATOR's own retransmit ladder (1,2,4,8...s), not a responder replay — no R2 replay expected or required.  Gate: counted netem-dropped >= 1 on the REQUEST direction AND the request logged strictly AFTER qdisc removal AND rekey completes (new SPI both sides) AND the NEW keymat carries g_ir_present=Y on BOTH sides with matching sha256 AND no followup timeout.  Completion with zero counted request loss proves nothing.  gate=box: box-only until a container run passes.

RFC 4945/6125 identity binding NEG: initiator holds a CA-valid cert with SAN-DNS x.r2-wild.test but ASSERTS IDi fqdn *.r2-wild.test; responder cert_validate on + ca_file + allow_wildcard_cert on and peers_id fqdn *.r2-wild.test (so the allowlist accepts the ID and only the cert binding guards).  Gate: chain validates ('X.509-from-wire: peer cert validated'), binding refuses ("asserted FQDN identity contains '*'"), NO child.

RFC 8784 PPK on the INITIAL IKE_SA (iked<->iked, USE_PPK both seats): SAi1 carries N(USE_PPK)=16435, responder echoes it, IKE_AUTH carries N(PPK_IDENTITY); both seats re-derive SK_d/SK_pi/SK_pr=prf+(PPK,SK') per RFC 8784 s4.2 and the ESP child landing proves the PPK-mixed keys matched on both sides. Kind asserts 'peer uses RFC 8784 PPK (USE_PPK)' on BOTH iked logs + 'responder confirmed PPK_IDENTITY' on the initiator (TRACE, -D 0x0003) plus the ADDKE intermediate round (SAi1 type-6 + 16438) that this kind always runs. PPK value = provisioned $SYSCONFDIR/ppk/rfc8784-mat.bin (32-byte sharing with the test peers; no fallback — iked fails closed if the file is missing) on both seats; secret files provisioned per-run, removed at cleanup. gate=box: container counted-gate PASS required before CI admission. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report (A1-A14/B-cells); a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

nine answered DPD intervals at dpd_delay 60, then initiator silence; responder must abort err=110 (retransmission count exceeded) with zero inbound UDP after the kill and no growth in dropping-unordered, unexpected-response, or CREATE_CHILD. gate=dpd: box-only (R2_DPD=yes); never part of the CI default. Not a NAT-D row. Classical ESP.

NDcPP A13 NEG (peer auth, fail-closed): responder holds the matrix PSK (macos.psk), initiator is pointed at a DIFFERENT existing psk file (l2tp.psk) — same fqdn ids, wrong key.  TOE must REFUSE: no ESP child AND responder iked logs authentication failure / AUTHENTICATION_FAILED.  The kind inverts the gate — returns 0 only when refused (a child means the TOE accepted a bad key).  gate=box: new row, container counted-gate PASS required before CI admission.

NDcPP A14 NEG (reference identifier, fail-closed): responder peers_id fqdn r2init-matrix, initiator presents a foreign my_id fqdn neg-intruder (same PSK).  TOE must REFUSE: no ESP child AND responder logs the ID_I does not match peers id rejection.  Inverted gate — 0 only when refused.  gate=box: new row, container counted-gate PASS required before CI admission.

NDcPP A12 STRICT (FCS_IPSEC_EXT.1.12): 256-bit CHILD_SA offered under a 128-bit IKE_SA with parent_child_strength on - TOE must refuse (NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN). Inverse-gate kind: exit 0 = refusal = PASS. gate=box, i2i topology (need netns+xfrm).

NDcPP A12 RFC-PERMISSIVE: same 256-bit child under 128-bit IKE_SA, parent_child_strength off (default) - RFC 7296 allows it, TOE must ACCEPT (child establishes). Positive gate. gate=box, i2i topology.

NDcPP A7/A8 CONF (admin-configurable lifetimes, notes 88/89): distinctive knobs kmp_sa_lifetime_time 37s (IKE_SA) + ipsec_sa_lifetime_time 53s (CHILD_SA); asserts the 53s reaches SADB as hard time (not default) AND an IKE_SA rekey fires inside the 37s soft window. gate=box (netns+xfrm), classical ESP, runs on any build.

IPv6 conformance (RFC 7296 over AF_INET6): iked<->iked on a veth with GLOBAL v6 addresses 2001:db8:1::1/::2 (NOT 192.0.x.x); IKEv2 transport, ESP AES-GCM tunnel SA and SADB all over IPv6. Proves the whole xfrm/SPD v6 path (sa_to_xaddr AF_INET6 branch, selectors /128, establish-sa inet6) — on a v4-only lib the SADB GETSPI fails with 'GETSPI addresses required'. Gate: ESP child up BOTH seats + CPL wired cells PASS + xfrm sel ::/0 template family both seats. gate=addke: box counted-gate + fedora:44 container counted-gate PASS 2026-10-01 (spmd/lib config.h INET6=1, both rows pass) -> CI-admitted (Fedora PQC matrix).

IPv6 conformance + RFC 4868 separate-integrity cipher over AF_INET6: same topology as i2iv6-esp but ESP uses aes128_cbc + hmac_sha2_256, proving the v6 SADB path carries a non-AEAD child cipher (enctype AES-CBC) end to end. Gate identical: ESP child up both seats + CPL PASS + xfrm sel ::/0. gate=addke: box counted-gate + fedora:44 container counted-gate PASS 2026-10-01 (spmd/lib config.h INET6=1, both rows pass) -> CI-admitted (Fedora PQC matrix).

IPv6-over-IPv4 tunnel (cross-matrix parity with freebsd-ci/i2io4-cbc128): IKE + outer ESP SA endpoints are v4 (192.0.5.1/::2, establish-sa inet), the PROTECTED selector is the v6 pair 2001:db8:1::1/::2 on the same veth — a v6 select=::/0 installed over a v4 template. The data-plane ping6 of the inner v6 MUST transit inside the v4 ESP tunnel (require SPD, no clear v6 path). Cleaner than i2iv6: the inner v6 is wrapped before output, so only v4 ARP (L2) is needed — no ND6 gate. Gate: ESP child up both seats + xfrm sel ::/0 over v4 SA + inner ping6 through the tunnel. Live box count 2026-10-16: the Linux xfrm backend previously dropped the v6 inner selector on the IKE child-SA install (fill_usersa saw no sp_src/sp_dst -> sel 0.0.0.0/0, policy could not bind, data plane dead); fixed at source in ikev2_child.c (selectors forwarded to sp_src/sp_dst when their family differs from the v4 SA endpoints) + A4 cipher cell + X6 regex. Both i2io4 rows now PASS live (box).

IPv6-over-IPv4 tunnel, AES-GCM child (cross-matrix parity with freebsd-ci/i2io4-gcm256): same topology as i2io4-cbc128 but esp_enc_alg aes_gcm / non_auth, proving the v6-selector-over-v4-template path carries an AEAD child. Gate identical: ESP child up both seats + xfrm sel ::/0 over v4 SA + inner ping6 through the tunnel. Live box count 2026-10-16: fixed with i2io4-cbc128 (ikev2_child.c Linux xfrm v6-selector forwarding); PASS live (box).

RFC 8784 PPK + AUTH-child PFS rekey TOGETHER, SELF-CONSISTENT iked<->iked (the production .mobileconfig shape: PPK AND EnablePFS=1 in one session) -- reworked from the dead -charon premise (strongSwan child DH = offer-not-requirement; charon never offers child DH at IKE_AUTH). BOTH iked seats set need_pfs on (new knob path: ike_conf.c honors it on the AUTH child + the responder records dhgrp from the matched AUTH-child pair) + use_ppk on with the provisioned rfc8784-mat PPK file on BOTH seats (fail-closed: no SHA-256 fallback; the file is provisioned per-run and removed at cleanup), short child lifetime (I2I_LIFETIME=25s) so an iked MINTS the child rekey mid-row; the rekey must carry the mirrored AUTH-child DH group (not the IKE SA's) AND the PPK-mixed SK_d stays valid. Gate: USE_PPK echo both seats + PPK_IDENTITY confirm + 'initiating CREATE_CHILD_SA rekey' + g_ir_present=Y post-rekey + ESP SPI change + no NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. gate=box. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

RFC 8784 PPK INTEROP: strongSwan charon 6.0.7 INITIATOR sends USE_PPK (IKE_SA_INIT) + the TYPED PPK_ID_FIXED (0x02) PPK_IDENTITY (rfc8784 5.1 slot), iked responder echoes USE_PPK, confirms PPK_IDENTITY and mixes the PPK into SK_d/SK_pi/SK_pr; the ESP child landing proves the PPK-mixed keys matched across two independent implementations (re-arbitrates racoon2's 5.1 type-octet fix against charon). Same ADDKE intermediate round as i2iinit-charon. Charon ppk secret = the shared provisioned 32 bytes $I2I_PPK_HEX (the same bytes iked provisions into $SYSCONFDIR/ppk/rfc8784-mat.bin; iked reads the file, no SHA-256 fallback) — the hex equals SHA-256('rfc8784-mat') but neither seat derives it; iked responder use_ppk on + charon ppk_required=yes (charon aborts if the PPK-mixed key mismatches) => ESTABLISHED proves the PPK. gate=addke (Fedora CI): container counted-gate PASS required before CI admission. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

RFC 8784 PPK INTEROP REVERSE: racoon2 iked INITIATES, strongSwan charon RESPONDER seat (-charonr) sends USE_PPK and answers the typed PPK_IDENTITY; iked confirms + mixes PPK, charon derives the same PPK-mixed SK_d; ESP child lands => cross-impl PPK match in the responder direction too. iked use_ppk on. Same ADDKE round. gate=addke (Fedora CI). Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

RFC 7296 2.18 AUTH-child PFS rekey, SELF-CONSISTENT iked<->iked (iPhone EnablePFS shape at IKE_AUTH: the initial child SA carries a DH group, which charon can never emit -- reworked from the dead -charon premise). BOTH iked seats set need_pfs on so the AUTH child is PFS-negotiated and child_sa->dhgrp records the matched group (the new ike_conf.c + ikev2_child.c path); RESPONDER short child lifetime (I2I_LIFETIME=25s) MINTS the child rekey; the fixed rekey must carry THAT group as KEi (ee60cda mirror, never borrow the IKE SA's dhdef) and the peer iked accepts (new ESP SPI) instead of NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. Gate: 'initiating CREATE_CHILD_SA rekey' + g_ir_present=Y post-rekey + ESP SPI change + no NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN either seat. Pre-feature: AUTH child was always DH-less, so the responder-minted rekey shipped KE-less and the PFS peer answered NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN (the live iPhone storm shape). gate=addke. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

AUTH-child PFS rekey with a DIFFERENT negotiated DH group, SELF-CONSISTENT iked<->iked (reworked from dead -charon). Same i2iinit-pfsrekey construction (need_pfs on both seats) but kmp_dh_group is ecp384 and the child esp proposal carries -ecp384, so the PFS-negotiated AUTH child uses ECP-384 and the responder-initiated rekey must carry a DH-20 KEi. Proves the AUTH-child DH-mirror is group-agnostic (carries the actual negotiated group into the rekey clone, not a hardcoded 19). Gate identical: iked mints the rekey, g_ir_present=Y post-rekey keymat, SPI change, no NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. gate=addke. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

AUTH-child PFS rekey with the THIRD negotiated DH group, SELF-CONSISTENT iked<->iked (reworked from dead -charon). Same construction but kmp_dh_group is ecp521 and the child esp proposal is -ecp521, so the PFS-negotiated AUTH child uses ECP-521 and the responder-initiated rekey must carry a DH-21 KEi. Proves the AUTH-child DH-mirror carries the actual negotiated group (ecp256, ecp384, ecp521) into the rekey clone, never a hardcoded 19. Gate identical: iked mints the rekey, g_ir_present=Y post-rekey keymat, SPI change, no NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. gate=addke. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

RFC 6023 INTEROP (Feature A): strongSwan charon 6.0.7 INITIATOR conn sets childless = force (swanctl childless_conn_lines), so charon sends a MODIFIED (SA-less) IKE_AUTH (no SAi2/TS). iked RESPONDER runs childless on (the new knob): advertises N(CHILDLESS_IKEV2_SUPPORTED)=16418 in the IKE_SA_INIT response, ACCEPTS the SA-less IKE_AUTH, answers SA-less (IDr/AUTH/notifies only), reaches ESTABLISHED with zero children, then charon adds the first CHILD_SA via a separate CREATE_CHILD_SA (strongSwan DOES offer child DH there). Gate: responder log has the 16418 advertise + the 'received childless (SA-less) IKE_AUTH' accept marker + ESP child UP (the CREATE_CHILD child) + both sides the ADDKE intermediate round. Proves the RFC 6023 responder childless path against a real second implementation. gate=box: container counted-gate PASS required before CI admission. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

RFC 6023 knob regression (iked<->iked): RESPONDER runs childless on; the racoon2 initiator has no childless-REQUEST support (SA-less AUTH is initiated by the peer in RFC 6023), so it sends a normal SA-full IKE_AUTH — the responder must still advertise 16418 on IKE_SA_INIT AND accept the classical AUTH normally, child lands. Gate: 16418 advertise marker on the responder log + ESP child UP + ADDKE round. Proves the new knob does not break the ordinary childful path. gate=addke. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

RFC 6023 childless + PFS rekey TOGETHER (the production shape that was unconstructible at IKE_AUTH): charon 6.0.7 INITIATOR conn childless = force sends a SA-less IKE_AUTH; iked responder childless on advertises 16418 + accepts it (ESTABLISHED, zero children); the FIRST child lands via a separate CREATE_CHILD_SA where strongSwan DOES offer child DH (esp_proposals aes128gcm16-ecp256), so the initial child is genuinely PFS-negotiated; then iked's short child lifetime (I2I_LIFETIME=25s, the -pfsrekey arm) MINTS the child rekey and it MUST carry the mirrored DH (ee60cda) — charon accepts (new ESP SPI) instead of NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. Gate = childless accept marker (16418 advertise + 'received childless (SA-less) IKE_AUTH') AND the pfsrekey gate (responder 'initiating CREATE_CHILD_SA rekey' + g_ir_present=Y post-rekey + SPI change + no NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN) AND the ADDKE round both sides. Replaces the four dead -pfsrekey*-charon premise rows with the legitimate childless path where charon really offers DH. gate=addke (Fedora CI). Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

Proposal shape: IKE_SA cipher AES-256-CBC (kmp_enc_alg aes256_cbc on both iked seats) instead of the base aes_gcm. RFC 9242 IntAuth_A requires an AEAD IKE cipher, so a CBC IKE_SA has no type-6/IKE_INTERMEDIATE round — this is a classical (non-ADDKE) row: the kind waives the PQC gate (need_pqc=0) and FAILS if any ADDKE round marker appears. Gate: ESP child UP + zero round markers + IKE_SA negotiated (ESTABLISHED). gate=box: new shape row, container counted-gate PASS required before CI admission. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

Proposal shape: IKE PRF + hash hmac_sha2_384 (kmp_prf_alg + kmp_hash_alg) on both iked seats; IKE cipher stays aes_gcm so the ADDKE/IKE_INTERMEDIATE round still runs (full PQC row, need_pqc=1). Gate: ESP child UP + both sides the round marker (same SK(1)) + no abort. Proves the PRF/HASH dimension of the proposal is independently negotiable without disturbing the PQC round. gate=box. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

Proposal shape: IKE PRF + hash hmac_sha2_512 on both iked seats; aes_gcm IKE keeps the ADDKE round live. Gate: ESP child UP + round marker both sides. Gate: ESP child UP + the SAD-shape gate (responder netns ip xfrm state shows aead rfc4106(gcm(aes)) keylen 32) + round marker + no abort. Proves a 256-bit AEAD child cipher negotiates. gate=box. Also runs the NDcPP v3.0e CPL compliance report; a wired-cell FAIL fails the case

Config option: ESP extended sequence numbers (ext_sequence on in the ipsec block, RFC 7296 §3.3.2 / RFC 4303 §2.2.1) on both iked seats. IMPLEMENTED: the offer carries ESN_YES+ESN_NO; a negotiated ESN_YES sets child_sa->esn (iked/ikev2_child.c) and the SA install lifts SADB_X_SAFLAGS_ESN (0x400; defined iked/if_pfkeyv2.h, set at iked/ikev2_child.c:2434, copied by lib/if_pfkeyv2.c) into the kernel SA. Proves the ESN flag rides a ChaCha AEAD SA (not just the GCM default) end-to-end into the Linux XFRM SADB. gate=box.

RFC 5723 session resumption INTEROP: Libreswan 5.x pluto INITIATOR in its own netns against the racoon2 iked RESPONDER (SUT) in the sibling netns. racoon2 mints N(TICKET_LT_OPAQUE) on the first IKE_AUTH (session_resumption on + ticket key); cond terminate -> re-initiate => pluto presents the stored ticket via IKE_SESSION_RESUME (exchange 38), racoon2 accepts it, derives the resumed keys, answers the resumed IKE_AUTH with prf(SK_pr,<message octets>), and BOTH SAs re-establish (Child ESP up) with NO full auth re-run. STRICT gate = the REAL resumed-session gate, not a partial exchange-38 Nr: resolver logs 'accepted IKE_SESSION_RESUME ticket, resumed keys derived, Nr sent' AND mints the ticket AND pluto logs 'authenticated peer using authby=session-resume' (the resume-pass-only line) AND 'established Child SA' AND responder ESP states >= 2 on BOTH passes (up1 AND up2, the pass-1 SAs drained before the resume pass). Requires libreswan pluto (session-resumption=yes) on the run host; gate=addke runs it on the box and the Fedora 44 container (dnf libreswan), Ubuntu (no ADDKE) and the non-xfrm FreeBSD vnet legs skip via the ADDKE gate.

RFC 5723 session resumption, self-consistent racoon2<->racoon2: the iked INITIATOR resumes a session from a ticket it stored on a prior IKE_AUTH (session_resumption on + ticket key on both seats, initiator persists to RACOON2_RESUME_TICKET_DIR), against the iked RESPONDER in the sibling netns. racoon2 mints N(TICKET_LT_OPAQUE) on the first IKE_AUTH; initiator restarted fresh (SA gone, store kept); re-establish => initiator presents the stored ticket via IKE_SESSION_RESUME (exchange 38), responder accepts it, derives the resumed keys, answers the resumed IKE_AUTH with prf(SK_pr,<message octets>), and BOTH SAs re-establish (Child ESP up) with NO full IKE_SA_INIT/AUTH re-run. STRICT gate = the REAL resumed-session gate, not a partial exchange-38 Nr: resolver logs 'accepted IKE_SESSION_RESUME ticket, resumed keys derived, Nr sent' AND mints the ticket AND the initiator's present branch fires ('resuming via IKE_SESSION_RESUME' on the fresh-restarted initiator) AND Child ESP >= 2 on BOTH passes (up1 AND up2). Requires session_resumption built in; gate=addke runs it on the box and the Fedora 44 container, and skips on the non-ADDKE Ubuntu head.

RFC 5723 s4.3.2 TICKET_NACK + fallback, racoon2<->racoon2: after a first IKE_AUTH stores a ticket, the RESPONDER rotates its session_resume_ticket_key; the initiator presents the old ticket; the responder must refuse it with N(TICKET_NACK) in an IKE_SESSION_RESUME (exchange 38) response; the initiator must keep the ticket, re-run a full IKE_SA_INIT + IKE_AUTH on the same SA (child up), and store the newly minted ticket. Gate: kfail + nack_sent(38) + nack_rcvd + fallback marker + IKE_SA_INIT state + up2, zero resume accepts, ticket record replaced.

RFC 5723 s4.3.1 reused-ticket rejection, racoon2<->racoon2: pass 2 resumes from the ticket the first IKE_AUTH stored (exactly one responder accept); pass 3 restarts the initiator with that SAME ticket restored into its store. The responder must refuse the second presentation (used-ticket cache, "ticket was already used") with N(TICKET_NACK) in exchange 38, and the initiator must fall back to a full IKE_SA_INIT + IKE_AUTH that brings the child up (up3).

RFC 5685 drain refuses ticketed resume (failover semantics, racoon2<->racoon2): after a first IKE_AUTH stores a ticket, the RESPONDER sets 'drain-sa <I> <gw>' (ikedctl, per-address drain).  A ticketed reconnect MUST NOT be resumed onto the node being drained (that would defeat the drain): the responder resume handler refuses it with N(TICKET_NACK); the initiator receives the NACK, keeps the stored ticket and falls back to a fresh (full) IKE_SA_INIT — which the draining node then N(REDIRECT)s, and redirect-follow migrates the ticket onto the sibling (N/A in this 2-seat row; the point is the refusal + fallback, not the landing).  Gate: drain-NACK marker 'IKE_SESSION_RESUME from drained peer refusing (TICKET_NACK)' in resp-iked.log + nack rcvd + fallback marker + INI_IKE_SA_INIT_SENT on the fresh restart, and ZERO resume accepts, on top of pass-1 child up + ticket minted.  Needs session_resumption + gate=addke.

RFC 5685 redirect to a LIVE sibling gateway (two-gateway, concentrator-shaped): THREE netns A(192.0.11.1)/I(192.0.11.2)/C(192.0.11.3) on a bridge hub; the child TRAFFIC SELECTOR targets the protected address 192.0.30.0 (a BARE address, parsed as /32 by rcs_getaddrlist) served identically by BOTH gateways — NOT a /24 subnet — and NO peers_sa_ipaddr/my_sa_ipaddr pin, so the tunnel endpoint auto-follows the redirect (ike_determine_sa_endpoint returns the retargeted remote). I->A up (esp>=2 both); A 'drain-sa <I> <C>' SILENTLY closes the SA (ikev2_abort, 'aborting ike_sa', A esp 2->0); I re-initiates to A -> N(REDIRECT,C); I verifies Ni and re-drives IKE_SA_INIT against the REAL C which completes a FULL IKE_AUTH + child (C esp>=2 AND I esp>=2) while A stays 0. Gate: I->A up; drain 'aborting ike_sa' + A esp 2->0; wire re-target '192.0.11.3[500]...INI_IKE_SA_INIT_SENT' in i-iked.log; C esp>=2 AND I esp>=2 AND A esp==0. NO data plane / no SPD row on the child (spmd_pfkey refuses a tunnel install without my_sa_ipaddr; same unpin that follows the redirect) — xfrm_audit.tsv declares traffic XFAIL; the proof is the failover LANDING. Honest: redirect+resume mutually exclusive at IKE_SA_INIT, so C completes full IKE_AUTH (migrate hook is a doc'd no-op). gate=box.

RFC 5685 s7 redirect-loop limit: gateways A and C statically redirect_to each other; the initiator (accept_redirect on, default redirect_max 5 / redirect_period 300) must follow the loop (exactly 1 initial + 5 followed IKE_SA_INIT sends: 3 to A, 3 to C), then log 'RFC5685 s7: redirect loop limit exceeded' and stop; no ESP SA on A or C.

RFC 5685 drain live rows (failover steps 4a+4b): iked<->iked child establishes; responder ikedctl 'drain-sa <peer> <gw>' then (4b) silently tears down the peer's ESTABLISHED IKE_SA (R esp 2->0, no DELETE on the wire — same quiet posture as delete-sa), and (4a) a NEW IKE_SA_INIT from the drained peer (now advertising REDIRECT_SUPPORTED/16406 per 8175b5a) is answered N(REDIRECT, gw) with the drain target and does NOT re-establish against the draining node. Gate: child UP first; R esp pruned 2->0 by drain-sa SET; initiator re-targets IKE_SA_INIT to the drain gateway (192.0.99.7 — wire evidence in init-iked.log, reachable only via the N(REDIRECT)+Ni-verify+retarget follow path) AND R esp stays 0 (client steered away). Promoted to CI 2026-10-24 after 3/3 consecutive passes in an isolated two-netns run (kernel 6.12).
